style_name: Extreme Industrial Protocols & Catastrophe SOPs (Clean 2D Digital Vector Cartoon Stickman)

voice.tone: investigative forensic interrogator, deliberate and measured countdown pace

acts.name: The Warning Beacon & Ticking Clock Hook
acts.goal: An analog meter shifts 2mm past the safe redline. Alarm beacon sirens blare. The 60-second ticking countdown clock begins.

acts.name: The Manual Mandate
acts.goal: Steps 1, 2, and 3 dictated by the heavy binder manual to prevent catastrophic explosion under extreme operator stress.

acts.name: The Mechanical Breakdown
acts.goal: Why emergency procedures failed: seized bypass valve, radio cross-talk, micro-corrosion on backup sensors, thermal cavitation cascade.

acts.name: The Industrial Legacy
acts.goal: Costly structural post-mortem, new safety regulations born from the disaster, and the haunting realization of modern infrastructure fragility.

flow.character_guide: Minimalist stickman technician with thin black stick limbs, a smooth off-white round head with expressive cartoon eyes, wearing an oversized bright yellow hard hat, safety goggles, and a clean orange utility vest with smooth color gradient shading.
flow.look: Clean 2D digital vector cartoon illustration, modern webcomic aesthetic, bold smooth black outlines, flat cel-shading with smooth vibrant color gradients, polished vector finish. Minimalist stickman technician with thin black stick limbs, a smooth off-white round head with expressive cartoon eyes, wearing an oversized bright yellow hard hat, safety goggles, and a clean orange utility vest with smooth color gradient shading. Industrial environment: rusted machine valves, analog gauge dials past the redline, damp reinforced concrete walls, single local dynamic light source from a flashing red industrial hazard beacon or warm amber alarm console casting radial glowing gradients onto surfaces and character. Layered atmospheric depth, clean cinematic composition. Single continuous 16:9 widescreen frame. Single camera view. Absolutely NO comic book panels, NO multi-panel grids, NO split screens, NO borders.

editorial.voice: Investigative technical forensic interrogator with quiet, measured deadpan wit. Pacing is deliberate with dramatic silent pauses right after delivering critical engineering metrics (bolt millimeters, steam PSI, fatigue micro-fractures). Never sensationalist. Explains mechanical dominos with visceral clarity.

hook_protocol.zero_fluff: Never open with pleasantries, 'Have you ever wondered', or historical intros.
hook_protocol.first_sentence: Sentence 1 (0:00-0:06) must present a specific gauge redline or emergency countdown timer. E.g., 'When this reactor pressure needle hits the redline, the binder manual on the console leaves exactly sixty seconds before four billion dollars of hardware vaporizes.'
hook_protocol.the_stakes: Line 0:06-0:30 establishes the catastrophic failure and domino chain if SOP is not executed.

rules: Zero fluff: start in second 1 with the critical micro-anomaly (a vibrating 12mm bolt, an overlooked pressure needle, a 4-degree oil temperature spike).
Micro-substance: cite exact engineering schematics, metallurgical micro-cracks, and specific manual log entries.
Everyday analogies: break down complex physics (cavitation, hydrogen embrittlement, harmonic resonance) into relatable physical mechanics.
Structure follows the second-by-second protocol: Warning Beacon -> Manual Mandate -> Mechanical Breakdown -> Industrial Legacy.

What Submarine Crews Are Ordered to Do When the Pressure Hull Breaches at 200m

composition_rules: Foreground Left (1/3 of frame): Close-up bust of stickman technician with oversized yellow hard hat and safety goggles, sweating or holding heavy wrench in panic
Background Right: Rusted industrial control console with screaming analog gauge needle past the redline and glowing red alarm beacon
Upper Third: Clean negative space for bold 2-3 word yellow text hook
STRICT: Absolutely NO text, words, letters, logos, banners in the image generation prompt

text_overlay_guide.words: 60 SECONDS? / CAN IT BLOW? / BREACH AT 200M
